project.name: tariff-rate-tracker
project.description: USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule data pipeline (R) producing statutory U.S. tariff rates at HTS-10 x country level, plus a React/Vite/Express duty-lookup frontend backed by DuckDB (local) and MotherDuck (cloud).

nodes.name: 00_build_timeseries.R
nodes.summary: Main R pipeline orchestrator that iteratively processes USITC HTS revisions to build the tariff rate time series, with full backfill, incremental, resume, and re-emit modes plus optional parallel fork workers and downstream invocation of weighted-ETR and quality stages.
nodes.languageNotes: R script invoked via Rscript; uses source(here(...)) to load every numbered pipeline stage and helpers as a single global environment.

nodes.name: 01_scrape_revision_dates.R
nodes.summary: Stage 01 of the pipeline: scrapes USITC HTS revision release dates and Chapter 99 PDF hashes, then upserts them into config/revision_dates.csv with change-detection logic.

nodes.name: 02_download_hts.R
nodes.summary: Stage 02 of the pipeline: builds USITC archive URLs and downloads missing HTS revision JSON archives into data/hts_archives, with size validation and idempotent skip-if-cached behavior.

nodes.name: 03_parse_chapter99.R
nodes.summary: Stage 03 of the pipeline: parses Chapter 99 special tariff provisions out of HTS JSON archives, extracting country lists, ch99 cross-references, and resolution status (active vs paused vs revoked).

nodes.name: 04_parse_products.R
nodes.summary: Stage 04 of the pipeline: parses individual HTS-10 product line items (descriptions, general/special/column2 rates, units, footnotes) out of the USITC JSON archives for one or all revisions.

nodes.name: preflight.R
nodes.summary: Standalone environment preflight validator: checks required and optional R packages, config files, resource files, and data directories before any pipeline run, exiting non-zero on missing required items.

nodes.name: install_dependencies.R
nodes.summary: Bootstrap script that installs all required and optional CRAN packages for the pipeline if they are not already present in the user library.

nodes.name: logging.R
nodes.summary: Lightweight leveled logging module exposing init_logging plus log_info / log_warn / log_error / log_debug helpers used by every pipeline stage.

nodes.name: scrape_us_notes.R
nodes.summary: Heavyweight scraper that downloads the Chapter 99 PDF from USITC and parses Section 301 product lists, floor-country exemptions, Note 36 copper products, and Note 16/19 derivative products, with anchor-coverage write-safety guards.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pdftools to OCR-free text-extract the Chapter 99 PDF; relies on anchor-text heuristics with a coverage threshold to avoid silently writing partial product lists.

nodes.name: helpers.R
nodes.summary: Central shared-utilities module sourced by nearly every pipeline stage: rate parsing, HTS code normalization, country/ISO mapping, parquet timeseries I/O, policy-params and revision-dates loaders, ch99 authority classification, schema enforcement, and stacking-rule logic.
nodes.languageNotes: 58 top-level functions in a single ~2,700-line file; functions are grouped by concern (rate parsing, country mapping, parquet I/O, policy loading, ch99 resolution, expiry adjustments) rather than split into modules.

nodes.name: build_full_timeseries
nodes.summary: Master orchestrator that walks every HTS revision in order, invoking the parse, calculate, validate, and emit stages and writing per-revision snapshot/delta/parquet outputs.

nodes.name: print_timeseries_summary
nodes.summary: Prints a human-readable summary of a built timeseries parquet, including row counts, revision span, and country/HTS coverage.

nodes.name: detect_incremental_start
nodes.summary: Inspects timeseries metadata to choose the next revision to process for an incremental build.

nodes.name: detect_resume_point
nodes.summary: mtime-aware crash recovery that finds the last fully-cached revision within the resume window so a killed run can pick up safely.

nodes.name: list_cached_revisions
nodes.summary: Diagnostic that lists every cached revision with its mtime and normalized-output status, used by --list-cached.

nodes.name: reemit_normalized_for_cached
nodes.summary: Re-emits Phase 2 normalized parquet outputs for already-cached revisions without re-running the heavy parse/calculate stages, optionally limited to stale tail.

nodes.name: api_name_to_revision
nodes.summary: Maps a USITC API release name (e.g. 'HTS Revision 28 (2025)') to a canonical revision ID like '2025_rev_28'.

nodes.name: fetch_usitc_releases
nodes.summary: Fetches the list of available HTS releases from the USITC API/website and returns them as a tibble with revision_id and effective_date.

nodes.name: update_revision_dates
nodes.summary: Upserts scraped USITC releases into config/revision_dates.csv, preserving manual overrides and supporting dry-run.

nodes.name: check_chapter99_pdf_changed
nodes.summary: Hashes the latest Chapter 99 PDF and compares it to the stored hash to detect whether US Notes need rescraping.

nodes.name: accept_chapter99_hash
nodes.summary: Persists a newly accepted Chapter 99 PDF hash to revision_dates.csv after a successful US Notes rescrape.

nodes.name: build_download_url
nodes.summary: Constructs the USITC HTS JSON archive download URL for a given revision and year.

nodes.name: download_hts_json
nodes.summary: Downloads a single HTS JSON archive to disk with size validation, treating partial downloads under min_size_mb as failures.

nodes.name: download_missing_revisions
nodes.summary: Iterates the revision_dates list, skips already-cached files, and downloads any HTS revision JSON archives missing from data/hts_archives.

nodes.name: parse_countries
nodes.summary: Parses the country list out of a Chapter 99 description string, distinguishing inclusion and exclusion clauses.

nodes.name: extract_country_names
nodes.summary: Extracts individual country names from a free-text fragment using a vocabulary of known names and aliases.

nodes.name: extract_ch99_references
nodes.summary: Pulls 9903.xx.xx cross-reference codes out of an HTS description string.

nodes.name: classify_resolution_status
nodes.summary: Classifies a Chapter 99 entry as active, paused, revoked, or pending based on its 9903 code and country-type signal.

nodes.name: parse_chapter99
nodes.summary: Top-level Chapter 99 parser that turns a USITC HTS JSON archive into a tibble of structured ch99 entries with countries, references, and status.

nodes.name: compare_chapter99
nodes.summary: Diffs two Chapter 99 parses (added, removed, changed entries) for revision-over-revision change reports.

nodes.name: parse_products
nodes.summary: Parses an HTS JSON archive into a tibble of HTS-10 product line items with description, general/special/column2 rates, unit of quantity, and footnotes.

nodes.name: parse_all_revisions
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that calls parse_products for every revision in a list and returns a named list of product tibbles.

nodes.name: compare_products
nodes.summary: Diffs two product parses to surface added, removed, and rate-changed HTS-10 codes between revisions.

nodes.name: check_packages
nodes.summary: Reports installed/missing status for a list of R packages, marking each as REQUIRED or OPTIONAL.

nodes.name: check_files
nodes.summary: Reports presence of a list of files relative to a base directory.

nodes.name: check_dirs
nodes.summary: Reports presence of required data/source/config directories and runs the dynamic local_paths.yaml resolution check.

nodes.name: install_if_missing
nodes.summary: Installs any CRAN packages from the given list that are not already available on .libPaths(), with a label distinguishing required vs optional batches.

nodes.name: init_logging
nodes.summary: Initializes the logger with an optional log file path and severity level threshold; stashes config in package-local options.

nodes.name: .log_write
nodes.summary: Internal log writer that timestamps a message, applies the level filter, and tees output to stderr and the log file.

nodes.name: download_chapter99_pdf
nodes.summary: Downloads the latest Chapter 99 PDF from USITC into data/us_notes, reusing a cached copy unless force is set.

nodes.name: extract_pdf_text
nodes.summary: Reads a PDF with pdftools and returns a per-page character vector for downstream anchor-based parsing.

nodes.name: find_product_list_anchors
nodes.summary: Locates Section 301 product list anchor headings (US Notes 20/31) in extracted PDF page text.

nodes.name: extract_hts_codes
nodes.summary: Extracts HTS subheading codes from a chunk of PDF text via regex.

nodes.name: extract_product_list
nodes.summary: Slices a page-range out of the PDF and returns the HTS codes between two anchor positions.

nodes.name: normalize_to_hts8
nodes.summary: Truncates and pads HTS codes of varying lengths to canonical HTS-8 form.

nodes.name: parse_us_note_products
nodes.summary: Top-level Section 301 parser that walks the Chapter 99 PDF, validates anchor coverage above 80%, and writes resources/s301_product_lists.csv.

nodes.name: find_floor_exempt_anchors
nodes.summary: Finds US Note 2 floor-country exemption category anchors (PTAAP, civil aircraft, pharmaceuticals) in extracted PDF text.

nodes.name: extract_inline_hts_codes
nodes.summary: Extracts HTS codes that appear inline (rather than in a block list) within US Note text.

nodes.name: parse_floor_exempt_products
nodes.summary: Parses US Note 2 floor-exempt products by category and writes resources/floor_exempt_products.csv with overwrite-safety guards.

nodes.name: parse_note36_copper_products
nodes.summary: Parses US Note 36 copper-content products covered by 9903.78.01 and refuses to overwrite resources/s232_copper_products.csv if fewer than ~60 codes are extracted.

nodes.name: parse_derivative_products
nodes.summary: Parses US Notes 16 and 19 Section 232 derivative-product lists (steel/aluminum derivatives) from the Chapter 99 PDF.

nodes.name: download_revision_chapter99_pdf
nodes.summary: Downloads the per-revision Chapter 99 PDF (used for revision-time-travel parsing of US Notes).

nodes.name: download_all_revision_pdfs
nodes.summary: Iterates the full revision list and downloads every per-revision Chapter 99 PDF that is missing locally.

nodes.name: parse_revision_floor_exemptions
nodes.summary: Runs the floor-exemptions parser against a single revision's Chapter 99 PDF, writing a per-revision resource file.

nodes.name: parse_all_revision_floor_exemptions
nodes.summary: Iterates all revisions and emits per-revision floor-exemption resource files, used to track the historical evolution of the exemption list.

nodes.name: parse_rate
nodes.summary: Parses a rate string from HTS into a numeric ad valorem rate (e.g. '6.8%' -> 0.068, 'Free' -> 0), returning NA for compound or specific rates.

nodes.name: is_simple_rate
nodes.summary: Predicate that returns TRUE only for simple ad-valorem or 'Free' rate strings parse_rate can safely convert.

nodes.name: normalize_hts
nodes.summary: Strips formatting from an HTS code and pads to a canonical zero-padded HTS-10 string.

nodes.name: parse_special_programs
nodes.summary: Parses an HTS 'special' rate column into a list of (program-code, rate) pairs (e.g. 'Free (A,AU,BH,...)').

nodes.name: parse_rate_extended
nodes.summary: Extended rate parser that returns numeric rate, rate type (ad-valorem / specific / compound), unit, and rounding rule.

nodes.name: parse_special_programs_multi
nodes.summary: Variant of parse_special_programs that handles multiple rate clauses (e.g. 'Free (A) 1% (B)') and returns one row per program.

nodes.name: load_census_codes
nodes.summary: Loads resources/census_codes.csv (Census trade partner codes used to join with USITC DataWeb).

nodes.name: load_country_partner_mapping
nodes.summary: Loads the Census <-> ISO partner-country crosswalk CSV used to harmonize country identifiers across data sources.

nodes.name: load_iso_countries
nodes.summary: Loads the canonical ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country list from the bundled JSON file.

nodes.name: normalize_country_name
nodes.summary: Normalizes free-text country names from HTS descriptions into canonical names matchable to the Census/ISO crosswalk, handling extensive aliases.

nodes.name: match_census_to_iso
nodes.summary: Joins Census trade partner codes onto ISO country codes via the partner-mapping crosswalk, surfacing unmatched rows.

nodes.name: open_rate_timeseries
nodes.summary: Opens the partitioned rate_timeseries Parquet dataset as an Arrow dataset for lazy querying.

nodes.name: query_rates
nodes.summary: Filters an open rate-timeseries Arrow dataset by countries, HTS codes, and date range, returning an in-memory tibble.

nodes.name: load_policy_params
nodes.summary: Loads and validates config/policy_params.yaml: section-by-section policy parameters (Section 232/301, IEEPA, floor exemptions, USMCA, expiry adjustments) with date coercion and defaulting.

nodes.name: get_country_constants
nodes.summary: Returns canonical Census codes for special-cased countries (China, Mexico, Canada, EU, Japan, S. Korea, etc.) used throughout the rate-calculation logic.

nodes.name: load_local_paths
nodes.summary: Loads config/local_paths.yaml and returns resolved absolute paths for optional external resources (TPC files, USMCA shares, etc.).

nodes.name: load_revision_dates
nodes.summary: Loads config/revision_dates.csv into a tibble with parsed effective_date and ch99 hash columns, validating revision IDs.

nodes.name: list_available_revisions
nodes.summary: Returns the list of revisions for which an HTS JSON archive exists locally for the requested year.

nodes.name: resolve_json_path
nodes.summary: Builds the on-disk JSON archive path for a given revision and year.

nodes.name: load_hts_concordance
nodes.summary: Loads resources/hts_concordance.csv: the year-over-year HTS-10 concordance used to bridge re-coded items across revisions.

nodes.name: remap_imports_via_concordance
nodes.summary: Remaps an imports-by-HTS panel through the HTS concordance so historical trade values stay attached to the new HTS-10 codes.

nodes.name: enforce_rate_schema
nodes.summary: Coerces a rate-output dataframe to the canonical schema (column names, types, ordering) used by the parquet writer.

nodes.name: apply_stacking_rules
nodes.summary: Applies the rate-stacking rules (mutual exclusion vs additive) across overlapping authorities (Section 232, 301, IEEPA, floor) for a given country and HTS-10.

nodes.name: compute_net_authority_contributions
nodes.summary: Decomposes the final stacked rate into per-authority net contributions for downstream attribution and dashboards.

nodes.name: parse_ch99_rate
nodes.summary: Parses the general rate text of a Chapter 99 entry into a numeric ad-valorem rate.

nodes.name: classify_authority
nodes.summary: Maps a 9903.xx.xx code to its underlying legal authority (Section 232 steel/aluminum, Section 301, IEEPA fentanyl/reciprocal, Section 122, etc.).

nodes.name: resolve_ch99_codes
nodes.summary: Joins Chapter 99 entries onto product rates by HTS-10 prefix and country, expanding ch99 cross-references and tagging each rate with its authority.

nodes.name: add_blanket_pairs
nodes.summary: Adds blanket country-coverage rate rows (e.g. IEEPA reciprocal floor that applies to all countries) by cross-joining covered HTS-10s with the country list.

nodes.name: load_232_derivative_products
nodes.summary: Loads resources/s232_derivative_products.csv: the steel/aluminum derivative product list with effective dates.

nodes.name: load_floor_exempt_products
nodes.summary: Loads resources/floor_exempt_products.csv: products exempt from the IEEPA reciprocal floor by country and category.

nodes.name: load_revision_floor_exemptions
nodes.summary: Loads the per-revision floor-exemption CSV emitted by parse_all_revision_floor_exemptions, used for revision-time-travel.

nodes.name: load_usmca_product_shares
nodes.summary: Loads (and optionally re-downloads from DataWeb) USMCA-eligible product shares used to weight Mexico/Canada compliant vs non-compliant rates.

nodes.name: load_metal_content
nodes.summary: Loads BEA-derived metal-content shares per HTS-10 used to compute the Section 232 copper-content rate (50% of metal content) by HTS-10.

nodes.name: apply_post_interval_adjustments_point
nodes.summary: Applies any policy expiry / scheduled-adjustment events that fall after a snapshot's effective date to a point-in-time query.

nodes.name: get_expiry_split_points
nodes.summary: Returns the set of dates within a snapshot validity window where a scheduled expiry would split the interval into sub-intervals.

nodes.name: apply_expiry_zeroing
nodes.summary: Zeros out (or steps down) rate components for an interval after a scheduled policy expiry takes effect.

nodes.name: get_rates_at_date
nodes.summary: Returns the effective tariff rates as of an arbitrary query_date, applying expiry-zeroing and post-interval adjustments to the underlying timeseries.

nodes.name: 05_parse_policy_params.R
nodes.summary: Pipeline stage 05 — parses policy parameters directly from HTS source data, extracting IEEPA reciprocal/fentanyl country rates from Chapter 99 headings (9903.01.43-75, 9903.02.xx), Section 232/122 base rates, and per-product USMCA eligibility into structured tibbles for the rate calculator.
nodes.languageNotes: R script using tidyverse + jsonlite; relies on country code constants loaded from config YAML via helpers.R.

nodes.name: 06_calculate_rates.R
nodes.summary: Pipeline stage 06 — the core rate calculator that builds the product × country tariff matrix per revision by stacking nine layers (footnote-based MFN, IEEPA reciprocal/fentanyl, Section 232 base + derivatives with metal scaling, Section 301, Section 122, MFN preference exemptions, USMCA carveouts, and stacking rules). Public entry point is calculate_rates_for_revision().
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy vectorized R logic with lazy sourcing of 07_emit_normalized.R for Phase 2 dual-write; 2447 lines reflect the full HTS regime stacking matrix.

nodes.name: 07_emit_normalized.R
nodes.summary: Pipeline stage 07 (dual-write) — emits the five-layer normalized rate schema (products_base, authority_country_rates, authority_product_applicability, authority_exemptions, plus revisions and country_group_membership statics) as parquet files alongside the legacy denormalized output, enabling Phase 2c parity validation before consumer cutover.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses arrow::write_parquet exclusively; reads the same in-memory intermediates as calculate_rates_for_revision() rather than deriving from final rates tibble to keep provenance explicit.

nodes.name: 07_validate_tpc.R
nodes.summary: Pipeline stage 07 (validation) — compares calculated tariff rates against Tax Policy Center benchmark estimates, summarizes discrepancies by country and chapter, and writes per-date comparison CSVs plus an overall validation summary to output/validation/.

nodes.name: 08_weighted_etr.R
nodes.summary: Pipeline stage 08 — computes import-weighted Effective Tariff Rates (ETRs) for all importing countries using 2024 Census import volumes, aggregating overall, by partner, by authority, and by GTAP sector with TPC overlay plots written to output/etr/.

nodes.name: 09_daily_series.R
nodes.summary: Pipeline stage 09 — broadcasts the interval-encoded rate timeseries to daily aggregates (overall, by country, by authority), supports on-demand expansion to daily product/country slices, and emits daily CSVs, parquets, and an Excel workbook plus alternative-scenario series via apply_scenarios.R.

nodes.name: build_country_lookup
nodes.summary: Builds a name-to-Census-code lookup from census_codes.csv augmented with HTS-text aliases (e.g., country shorthand variants) for matching country names found in HTS descriptions.

nodes.name: extract_countries_from_description
nodes.summary: Parses free-text HTS descriptions to extract referenced country names using regex and known country aliases, handling EU-27 expansion and special phrasings.

nodes.name: match_countries
nodes.summary: Maps a vector of extracted country names to Census codes via the lookup table, returning matched codes and unmatched names for diagnostic logging.

nodes.name: extract_ieepa_rates
nodes.summary: Extracts IEEPA reciprocal country rates from Chapter 99 headings (9903.01.43 through 9903.01.75), parsing rate values, effective date phases, and applicable countries into a per-country phase-keyed tibble.

nodes.name: extract_ieepa_fentanyl_rates
nodes.summary: Extracts IEEPA fentanyl-justification country rates (9903.02.xx) for Canada, Mexico, and China, including phase-specific rate transitions.

nodes.name: extract_section232_rates
nodes.summary: Extracts Section 232 (national security) base rates and derivative-product rates from Chapter 99 entries — covering steel, aluminum, autos, copper, lumber, and other 232 actions with effective-date phases and country exemptions.

nodes.name: extract_section122_rates
nodes.summary: Extracts Section 122 (balance-of-payments) blanket-tariff parameters from Chapter 99 entries.

nodes.name: is_232_exempt
nodes.summary: Predicate determining whether a Census country code is in the Section 232 exempt list for a given action category.

nodes.name: extract_usmca_eligibility
nodes.summary: Extracts per-HTS10 USMCA eligibility from the 'special' field of HTS records, normalizing CA/MX preference indicators into a clean eligibility table.

nodes.name: calculate_rates_fast
nodes.summary: Vectorized footnote-based rate calculator that resolves HTS Chapter 99 cross-references (e.g., 9903.88.xx for 301, 9903.01.xx for IEEPA) into per-product additional rates by stacking method.

nodes.name: check_country_applies
nodes.summary: Predicate determining whether a tariff measure applies to a given country given its country_type qualifier (e.g., 'all', 'except', 'only-listed') and exempt-country list.

nodes.name: apply_232_derivatives
nodes.summary: Applies Section 232 derivative-product rates including metal-content scaling — multiplies the 232 rate by per-product steel/aluminum content shares, handles UK quota exemptions, and merges into the rates tibble.

nodes.name: calculate_rates_for_revision
nodes.summary: Public entry point that runs the full nine-step rate calculation for a single HTS revision: footnote MFN, IEEPA reciprocal/fentanyl with SCOTUS-invalidation cutoff, Section 232 base + derivatives, Section 301, Section 122, MFN preference adjustments, floor recomputation, USMCA exemptions, and stacking rules. Triggers 07_emit_normalized.R dual-write.

nodes.name: emit_products_base
nodes.summary: Emits the products_base.parquet layer (HTS10 catalog with revision_id, MFN base rate, USMCA eligibility, and metal-content fields) for a given revision.

nodes.name: emit_authority_country_rates
nodes.summary: Emits authority_country_rates.parquet — country-level rate rows per authority (IEEPA reciprocal/fentanyl, Section 232 base, Section 122) with phase boundaries.

nodes.name: emit_authority_product_applicability
nodes.summary: Emits authority_product_applicability.parquet — per-(authority, hts10) rows describing which products fall within each tariff regime, including Section 232 derivatives, Section 301 product lists, and metal-content scaling factors.

nodes.name: emit_authority_exemptions
nodes.summary: Emits authority_exemptions.parquet — IEEPA product exemptions, IEEPA floor exemptions, Section 232 country exemptions, and Section 122 Annex II exemptions in a unified schema.

nodes.name: emit_normalized_revision
nodes.summary: Per-revision orchestrator — sequences emit_products_base, emit_authority_country_rates, emit_authority_product_applicability, emit_authority_exemptions, and emit_product_metal_content_rev for one revision into output/normalized/{revision}/.

nodes.name: emit_product_metal_content_rev
nodes.summary: Emits per-revision product_metal_content slice with steel/aluminum content shares used for Section 232 derivative scaling.

nodes.name: emit_normalized_statics
nodes.summary: One-shot emitter for revision-invariant tables — revisions.parquet, product_metal_content.parquet, country_group_membership.parquet, plus MFN and country-group reference tables.

nodes.name: create_country_name_map
nodes.summary: Builds a name-to-code map from census_codes for translating TPC's free-text country names into Census codes used by the calculated rates.

nodes.name: load_tpc_data
nodes.summary: Loads and pivots TPC tariff_by_flow_day.csv into a long (country, hts10, date, rate) tibble, mapping country names through the name-to-code map.

nodes.name: compare_to_tpc
nodes.summary: Joins our calculated rates to TPC benchmarks at a target date, computing per-row differences and classifying matches/discrepancies.

nodes.name: summarize_by_country
nodes.summary: Aggregates the validation comparison by country, reporting match counts and mean absolute rate differences.

nodes.name: summarize_by_chapter
nodes.summary: Aggregates the validation comparison by HTS chapter for chapter-level discrepancy analysis.

nodes.name: identify_discrepancies
nodes.summary: Splits the comparison into large_diff, missing_in_ours, and extra_in_ours categories for targeted CSV output.

nodes.name: validate_revision_against_tpc
nodes.summary: Per-revision validation orchestrator — loads TPC data for the given date, runs compare_to_tpc plus all summarizers, and returns a structured validation report.

nodes.name: run_validation
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point that runs validation across all dates with TPC coverage and writes per-date comparison CSVs, large-diff CSVs, missing/extra CSVs, and an overall validation_summary.csv.

nodes.name: load_data
nodes.summary: Loads the input bundle for ETR computation — products, IEEPA rates, USMCA eligibility, partner mapping, and 2024 Census import volumes from configured paths.

nodes.name: load_tpc_data
nodes.summary: Loads TPC benchmark rates (tariff_by_flow_day.csv) for overlay comparison with our weighted ETRs.

nodes.name: aggregate_tpc
nodes.summary: Aggregates TPC rates by partner using GTAP import weights to produce partner-level TPC ETRs that match our aggregation grain.

nodes.name: enrich_policy_dates_with_overrides
nodes.summary: Adds policy-parameter date overrides (e.g., effective-date adjustments from config/policy_params.yaml) to the policy-dates tibble used for ETR snapshots.

nodes.name: compute_weighted_etrs
nodes.summary: Computes per-revision import-weighted ETRs across all (HTS10, country) pairs by joining rates to 2024 Census import values and weighting by import dollars.

nodes.name: aggregate_etrs
nodes.summary: Aggregates weighted ETRs into four cuts: overall, by partner group, by tariff authority, and by GTAP sector.

nodes.name: plot_etrs
nodes.summary: Generates ETR time-series plots (overall, partner, authority, sector) with TPC overlay comparison and writes PNGs to the output directory.

nodes.name: run_weighted_etr
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point that loads inputs, runs compute_weighted_etrs and aggregate_etrs, generates plots, and writes per-cut CSVs to output/etr/.

nodes.name: build_daily_aggregates
nodes.summary: Computes daily aggregate ETRs (overall, by country, by authority) from the interval-encoded rate timeseries by computing one aggregate per revision and broadcasting across calendar days within each revision's validity window.

nodes.name: expand_to_daily
nodes.summary: On-demand expansion of the interval-encoded timeseries to a per-day (date, hts10, country) tibble for a specified date range and slice of countries/products.

nodes.name: export_daily_slice
nodes.summary: Materializes a daily slice to disk in parquet (preferred) or CSV format at the requested grain for downstream consumers.

nodes.name: load_import_weights
nodes.summary: Loads 2024 Census import-weight RDS for use as the weighting basis in daily ETR aggregates.

nodes.name: save_daily_workbook
nodes.summary: Writes the daily aggregates to a multi-sheet Excel workbook for stakeholder distribution.

nodes.name: build_daily_workbook_readme
nodes.summary: Constructs the README sheet content for the daily Excel workbook describing each sheet's columns and methodology.

nodes.name: save_daily_outputs
nodes.summary: Writes daily_overall.csv, daily_by_country.csv, daily_by_authority.csv, and daily_aggregates.rds to the output directory.

nodes.name: run_daily_series
nodes.summary: Top-level pipeline wrapper that builds daily aggregates from a timeseries and saves all standard daily outputs.

nodes.name: save_alternative_output
nodes.summary: Writes a scenario-variant daily_overall CSV under a variant-specific filename.

nodes.name: build_alternative_timeseries
nodes.summary: Rebuilds the rate timeseries under an alternative policy-parameter override (counterfactual scenario) by re-sourcing stages 03-06 with an overridden policy_params and applying scenarios via apply_scenarios.R.

nodes.name: run_alternative_series
nodes.summary: Orchestrator that iterates over a list of scenario variants, rebuilding each variant's timeseries and emitting alternative daily_overall outputs.

nodes.name: apply_scenarios.R
nodes.summary: Applies named scenario overrides (loaded from config/scenarios.yaml) to a base statutory-rate timeseries and supports A/B comparison of scenarios.
nodes.languageNotes: R script driven by a YAML scenario catalog; functions return modified copies of the rate panel rather than mutating in place.

nodes.name: build_hts_concordance.R
nodes.summary: Builds a cross-revision HTS-10 concordance by computing Jaccard similarity between dropped and added codes and classifying changes (split, merge, rename, simple add/drop).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses pairwise Jaccard similarity over tokenized HTS descriptions to match codes across USITC HTS revisions.

nodes.name: compare_etrs.R
nodes.summary: Imperative comparison harness that diffs this repo's ETR (effective-tariff-rate) outputs against external benchmarks and emits comparison tables.
nodes.languageNotes: Top-level script (no function definitions) that loops over benchmark files via map_dfr and writes comparison results.

nodes.name: denorm_state_contract.R
nodes.summary: Schema/validator for the denormalized policy state object — checks IEEPA, Section 232, Section 301, Section 122 and product-annex shapes before downstream rate calculation.
nodes.languageNotes: Internal R validator helpers prefixed with a dot (.validate_*) compose into validate_denorm_state with strict/loose modes.

nodes.name: diagnose_china_gap.R
nodes.summary: Diagnostic script that investigates China-specific tariff coverage gaps between this repo's panel and reference benchmarks (TPC / Yale Budget Lab).

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the top-level README to anchor on what this repo actually produces: a revision-by-revision interval-encoded tariff panel at the HTS-10 x country level, plus daily aggregate series and weighted Effective Tariff Rates derived from it. The README also lists the pointers you will follow in the rest of the tour - methodology, build, MotherDuck ops - and sketches the two halves of the system: an R data pipeline under src/ and a React/Vite/Express duty-lookup app under frontend/.

tour.title: Methodology and Calculation Logic
tour.description: Before reading any code, ground yourself in the conceptual model. methodology.md walks the U.S. tariff regime history (Section 122, 232, 301, IEEPA, USMCA) and explains which authority each piece of code models. CALCULATION_LOGIC.md is the canonical specification for the nine-layer duty-stack algorithm - footnote-based MFN, IEEPA, Section 232/301/122, USMCA, stacking, and finalization - and is the contract that both the R pipeline (Step 7) and the in-browser TypeScript calculator (Step 12) implement.

tour.title: Setup and Build
tour.description: build.md is the runnable companion to the README, walking first-time users through R 4.3+ and system prerequisites, dependency installation, and the end-to-end timeseries build. preflight.R is the standalone gatekeeper: it verifies required and optional R packages, config files, resource files, and data directories before any pipeline run, exiting non-zero if anything is missing. install_dependencies.R bootstraps the CRAN packages preflight checks for. Together these are the smallest viable surface for getting the pipeline runnable on a fresh machine.

tour.title: The Pipeline Orchestrator
tour.description: 00_build_timeseries.R is the heart of the data pipeline - the main R orchestrator that iteratively processes USITC HTS revisions to build the tariff rate timeseries. It supports full backfill, incremental, resume, and re-emit modes, optional parallel fork workers, and dispatches the downstream weighted-ETR and quality stages. Reading this file gives you a map of stages 01 through 09 - the same numbered stages the rest of the tour walks one by one. From the structural analysis, this file directly source()s every stage you are about to meet.
tour.languageLesson: R has no module system. Files share code via source(), which executes the target script in the current environment - any function or variable it defines becomes available to the caller. That is why the orchestrator can dispatch into stages 01-09 without an import statement, and why src/helpers.R (Step 7) is sourced by nearly every other R file: every stage just re-runs source('src/helpers.R') at startup.

tour.title: Data Acquisition (Stages 01-02)
tour.description: Stage 01 scrapes USITC HTS revision release dates and Chapter 99 PDF hashes, upserting them into config/revision_dates.csv with change-detection logic so we know which revisions exist and when they took effect. Stage 02 then builds USITC archive URLs and downloads any missing HTS revision JSON archives into data/hts_archives, with size validation and idempotent skip-if-cached behavior. Together these two stages turn 'a list of dates' into 'a folder of raw HTS JSON' that everything downstream parses.

tour.title: Parsing the Raw HTS (Stages 03-05)
tour.description: Stages 03-05 turn raw USITC JSON into structured tibbles the rate engine can consume. Stage 03 parses Chapter 99 special tariff provisions, extracting country lists, ch99 cross-references, and resolution status (active vs paused vs revoked). Stage 04 parses individual HTS-10 product line items - descriptions, general/special/column2 rates, units, footnotes - per revision. Stage 05 extracts policy parameters directly from HTS source data: IEEPA reciprocal/fentanyl country rates from Chapter 99 headings, Section 232/122 base rates, and USMCA eligibility flags. policy_params.yaml is the human-edited source-of-truth file that stage 05 reconciles against - 27 sections covering country codes, IEEPA flags, Section 232/301 product lists, USMCA carveouts, floor rates, and validation thresholds.
tour.languageLesson: YAML uses indentation for hierarchy and is forgiving about quoting - the same key can hold a scalar, a list, or a nested map. policy_params.yaml exploits this to bundle 27 logically distinct policy sections in one human-editable file, then the R parser reads it once and dispatches each section to a typed loader in helpers.R (Step 7).

tour.title: The Rate Engine (Stage 06 + Shared Helpers)
tour.description: Stage 06 is the core of this entire codebase - the rate calculator that builds the product x country tariff matrix per revision by stacking nine layers: footnote-based MFN, IEEPA reciprocal/fentanyl, Section 232 base plus derivatives with metal scaling, Section 301, Section 122, MFN preference exemptions, USMCA carveouts, and stacking rules. Its public entry point is calculate_rates_for_revision(). It rests on src/helpers.R - the highest-fan-in node in the entire graph (33 incoming edges) - which centralizes rate parsing, HTS code normalization, country/ISO mapping, parquet timeseries I/O, policy-params loaders, ch99 authority classification, schema enforcement, and stacking-rule logic. Almost every other R file source()s helpers.R at startup.

tour.title: Output Emission (Stages 07-09)
tour.description: Once stage 06 has produced the rate matrix, stages 07-09 emit it in every shape downstream consumers need. Stage 07 dual-writes the five-layer normalized rate schema (products_base, authority_country_rates, authority_product_applicability, authority_exemptions, plus revisions and country_group_membership statics) as parquet alongside the legacy denormalized output. Stage 08 computes import-weighted Effective Tariff Rates using 2024 Census import volumes - overall, by partner, by authority, and by GTAP sector - and writes TPC overlay plots to output/etr/. Stage 09 broadcasts the interval-encoded panel to daily aggregates (overall, by country, by authority), supports on-demand expansion to daily product/country slices, and emits daily CSVs, parquets, and an Excel workbook. This is where the README's promise of 'daily series and weighted ETRs derived from the panel' actually gets fulfilled.

tour.title: Tests and TPC Validation
tour.description: Two layers of correctness sit on top of the pipeline. test_rate_calculation.R is the unit-test suite - roughly 50 test cases covering Chapter 99 parsing, IEEPA/Section 232/Section 122/USMCA fixtures, total_rate decomposition, and the 232/IEEPA mutual-exclusion stacking rule that the engine has to get exactly right. 07_validate_tpc.R is a parallel validation pass that compares calculated tariff rates against Tax Policy Center benchmark estimates, summarizes discrepancies by country and chapter, and writes per-date comparison CSVs plus an overall summary to output/validation/. Together they answer 'does the rate engine match the spec?' and 'does the rate engine match the outside world?'

tour.title: From Pipeline to Frontend
tour.description: The R pipeline produces parquet files; the frontend needs them in MotherDuck and in the browser. prepare_frontend_data.R is the bridge script that exports parquet/JSON datasets from the R pipeline output directory into frontend/public/data/ for the React app to consume directly. push-to-motherduck.mjs is the cloud-side counterpart: it reads the normalized parquet from output/normalized/, full-rebuilds or incrementally replaces the MotherDuck rates table per revision, and rebuilds the product_base_rates materialized table in batches to avoid Pulse duckling OOMs. MOTHERDUCK.md is the operations runbook tying it all together - db push commands, the batched rebuild, schema evolution, and Railway deploy steps.

tour.title: Frontend API Server
tour.description: frontend/server.js is the Express API backing the duty-lookup UI; it wires DuckDB-Node and MotherDuck connections, an LRU rates cache, gap-filling synthesis, and HTS description indexing behind /api/rates, /api/rates/batch, /api/products, /api/health, and an Arrow IPC streaming endpoint. server/db.js is the connection layer underneath - it initializes either DuckDB-Node against the local parquet dataset or the MotherDuck cloud client and exposes the rates projection plus the product_base_rates view definition the API queries. This is the seam between the pipeline's output (Step 10) and everything that runs in the user's browser.
tour.languageLesson: Node ESM modules import via static `import` syntax with `.js`/`.mjs` extensions, but server.js is plain CommonJS while push-to-motherduck.mjs (Step 10) is an ES module - the `.mjs` extension forces ESM mode regardless of package.json. This split lets the long-running Express server keep CommonJS's faster startup while the one-shot data-loader script gets top-level await for clean async sequencing.

tour.title: Frontend Client and the In-Browser Calculator
tour.description: main.tsx is the React entry - it creates the root, imports Tailwind globals, and mounts <App/> into #root. App.tsx is the root component: it renders the SAIL Duty Rate Calculator chrome (header, footer, coverage badges), wires in dataset stats from useDataStats, and mounts the DutyLookupModule (the highest-fan-out node in the graph at 10 outgoing edges, the entry point to the entire duty-lookup feature). tariffCalculator.ts is the keystone: it mirrors the R pipeline's resolve_rate_normalized logic in TypeScript, applying the same stacked tariff regimes (MFN, IEEPA, Section 232/301, reciprocal) from Step 7 to compute landed cost, MPF, HMF, and per-authority duty amounts for a single (HTS-10, country, date) query. This is why the methodology in Step 2 was load-bearing: two implementations of the same nine-layer algorithm, one in R for batch panels and one in TS for sub-millisecond browser lookups, must agree.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript uses ES module resolution with explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` source extensions that the Vite bundler rewrites to `.js` at build. Import paths without extensions resolve through tsconfig's module-resolution rules - `frontend/tsconfig.json` declares the path aliases (e.g. `@/`) that let `import { calculateDuty } from '@/utils/tariffCalculator'` work everywhere in the React tree without relative-path spelunking.
